references.text: The context for this verse: Jesus has just told the disciples not to worry about what they will eat or wear, for life is more than food ([ref:Luk 12:22-23|Luke 12:22-23]).
The parallel passage in the Sermon on the Mount where Jesus says that the disciples should not worry about what they will eat or drink ([ref:Matt 6:25|Matthew 6:25]).

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says that the disciples should not ask, "What shall we eat?" or "What shall we drink?", for it is the Gentiles who seek after all these things ([ref:Matt 6:31-32|Matthew 6:31-32]).
Paul urges believers not to worry about anything, but in everything to present their requests to God ([ref:Fil 4:6|Philippians 4:6]).
Peter encourages believers to cast all their anxiety on God, for he cares for them ([ref:1 Pet 5:7|1 Peter 5:7]).
The psalmist urges us to cast our burden on the Lord, for he will sustain us ([ref:Sal 55:23|Psalm 55:23]).

The direct continuation of the verse, where Jesus justifies the exhortation by saying that the Father knows what they need, and urges them to seek his kingdom instead ([ref:Luk 12:30-31|Luke 12:30-31]).
An encouragement to commit your way to the Lord and trust in him – he will do it ([ref:Sal 37:5|Psalm 37:5]).
The Lord says, "Do not fear, for I am with you", a fundamental assurance of God's care that underlies Jesus' exhortation against anxiety ([ref:Jes 41:10|Isaiah 41:10]).
